description: Missing `set -euo pipefail` and `shopt -s inherit_errexit` strict mode per BCS0101.
Function variables not declared `local`; pollutes global scope per BCS0202.
Word-splits a string into an array and iterates with unquoted `${arr[@]}` per BCS0206 anti-pattern.
Uses legacy backtick command substitution instead of `$(...)` per BCS0302.
RHS of `=~` is quoted, which disables regex matching per BCS0303.
Uses single-bracket `[ ... ]` conditionals on strings and numbers; BCS0501 mandates `[[ ... ]]` and `(( ... ))`. (File tests in `[ ]` belong to BCS0901.)
Pipes into `while read`, creating a subshell that loses variable mutations; BCS0504 is the canonical code for pipe-to-while (BCS0503 and BCS0903 defer to it).
Critical `mv` and `cp` invocations have no `|| die` guard or context message per BCS0604.
Error messages written to stdout instead of stderr per BCS0702.
Option `-o` captures `$1` after `shift` without a `noarg` check; missing argument silently corrupts state per BCS0803.
Uses `test -f` / `test -r` instead of `[[ -f ... ]]` / `[[ -r ... ]]` per BCS0901.
Globs without `./` path prefix; a file named `-rf` could hijack commands as flags per BCS0902.
Script calls external commands without hardening PATH at start per BCS1002.
Uses `eval` for dynamic function dispatch where a `case` statement would be safer per BCS1004.
Hardcoded `/tmp/<name>_$$` temp path is predictable per BCS1006; should use `mktemp`.
Creates a temp directory with `mktemp -d` but installs no `trap` for cleanup per BCS0110.
Ad-hoc `[[ $# -gt 0 ]]` with `if/elif` argument parsing instead of the BCS0801 `while (($#)); do case` pattern.
Pipes `find` output into a while loop; BCS0504 mandates `< <(command)` process substitution to preserve variables.
`((flag)) && action` chains without trailing `||:`; under `set -e`, script exits when the flag is zero per BCS0606.
Background jobs launched with `&` but their PIDs are never captured or waited on (BCS1101).
Recursive walk uses loop variable `entry` without `local`; recursion corrupts the caller's value (BCS0410).
Bash version gate uses one compound `&&` over major/minor; wrongly rejects Bash 6.0 (BCS0409).
Script sets the SUID bit on itself; SUID on Bash scripts is forbidden (BCS1001).
No shebang at all; the first line of a script must be one of the three accepted bash shebangs per BCS0102. The shellcheck shell= directive only keeps the linter usable.
Dual-purpose script applies `set -euo pipefail` above the source fence, so sourcing it alters the caller's shell; strict mode belongs below the fence per BCS0406.
Pure function library with no guard against direct execution; a library must reject being run per BCS0407.
Disables strict mode with `set +e` around a command that may fail, instead of handling the failure explicitly per BCS0601.
Trap command in double quotes expands `$TEMP_FILE` when the trap is installed (still empty), so the temp file is never removed; trap commands must be single-quoted per BCS0603.
A caller-supplied name is joined to a base directory and removed with no validation, so `../..` escapes the base (BCS1005).
Waits on tracked background jobs with `wait "$pid" ||:`, discarding every exit code so failed jobs go unnoticed; failures must be accumulated per BCS1103.
Fully BCS-compliant minimal script; any finding is a false positive.
Fully BCS-compliant integer summation; any finding is a false positive.
Fully BCS-compliant non-blank line counter via redirect; any finding is a false positive.
Realistic compliant CLI tool (metadata, messaging, noarg, bundled options, flag-guarded actions, readonly after parse, default case arm, #fin); any finding is a false positive.

Compliant report script with argument parsing in its own function outside main(), locals assigned well after their declaration, a canonical path before find, and a cleanup trap installed before mktemp; any finding is a false positive.
Short compliant script with top-level logic and no functions (allowed under ~200 lines): typed globals, inline-IFS read, quoted heredoc, builtin date formatting; any finding is a false positive.
Parses a version tag with external grep/cut instead of [[ =~ ]] + BASH_REMATCH (BCS0507, recommended).
Assigns through a variable name with eval instead of a `local -n` nameref. BCS1004 owns eval avoidance and is the canonical code; BCS0210 names the nameref alternative.
A `#shellcheck disable=SC2155` directive with no reason given, on the line or above it, violating BCS1206's documented-exceptions requirement.
Installs a PATH-wide executable under a `.sh` name; globally available executables must have no extension per BCS0106.
Network fetch via curl with no timeout; a hung server stalls the script indefinitely (BCS1104).
die() is defined, yet one failing exit below it hand-rolls `echo ...; exit 22` instead of calling it (BCS0602).
Help is printed through info(), which VERBOSE gates, so `-q -h` prints nothing (BCS0704).
